review.summary: OpgG's core molecular function is inferred to be beta-1,2-glucanase activity.
review.reason: Primary biochemical and structural work on E. coli OpgG/OpgD-family orthologs supports GH186 beta-1,2-glucanase activity, and the P. putida protein has strong sequence, domain, signal-peptide, and opgGH operon support for ISS transfer of the same periplasmic OPG-processing role.

supported_by.supporting_text: EcOpgG was found to hydrolyze β-1,2-glucans; however, the catalytic velocity was very low
EcOpgG also showed the same substrate specificity toward the polysaccharides as that of EcOpgD.

Global Needleman–Wunsch alignment of Q88D03 (559 aa) gave **63.6% identity (357/561 aligned positions)** to the biochemically and structurally characterized E. coli OpgG (P33136) and **66.4% identity (383/577)** to P. aeruginosa OpgG (Q9HUA5).
The exact in-vivo cut/branch chemistry OpgG performs during OPG maturation remains to be pinned down, but the enzyme class is now defined.
